verdict: LEXICAL PROXIMITY OF RELATED TOPICS; NO SUBSTANTIVE NEIGHBOR LEAK FOUND. Q9 remains specifically about applying Test-First; Q6 is about defining TDD and its Red-Green-Refactor cycle. They intentionally share core concepts, which explains the higher lexical match to Q6.

expected_scope: Observe expected red and diagnose cause
q9_question_parts.assessment: Question is actionable and narrower than Q6 definition/cycle question.

A.scope: Directly answers how to implement Test-First.

B.truth: Wrong; confuses new feature with behavior-preserving refactor.
B.scope: Plausible distractor on how to proceed to next behavior.

D.truth: Wrong; skips observed red and overclaims what green proves.

q9_sections_assessment.detail: Correct answer sections explain the practice and its limits. Wrong answer sections explain why each wrong model fails and how the sequence should work. CI/quality gates appear only as a boundary clarification, not as a competing answer theme.

q9_theory_assessment.focus: Test-First sequence, selected cases, practical example, and distinction between final code and evidence of process.
q9_theory_assessment.overlap_with_q6: Expected Red, Green, behavior-preserving Refactor, and test limits are shared terminology/concepts.
q9_theory_assessment.distinctive_content: Validator example, choosing/adding cases, sequencing in legacy code, and explicit process-vs-final-code distinction are Q9-specific.

q6_theory_assessment.focus: Definition of TDD and explanation of cycle, with price calculator example and Martin three-law framing.
q6_theory_assessment.overlap_with_q9: Test precedes behavior implementation; expected cause of Red; Green; preserving behavior during Refactor; limits of green suite.
q6_theory_assessment.distinctive_content: TDD/API design framing, pricing example, parameterized tests, BigDecimal note, VIP feature boundary, three laws, and broader cycle discussion.

comparison.shared_concepts: Expected overlap is substantial because Test-First is a core practice within TDD and both questions discuss the same red/green/refactor feedback sequence. Similar vocabulary is semantically appropriate.
comparison.material_difference: Q9 asks for an actionable Test-First method; Q6 asks what TDD is and what its cycle means. Q9 distractors test sequence errors; Q6 distractors test conceptual stage errors. The explanations/examples also differ.
comparison.scanner_interpretation: Coverage similarity alone does not establish content drift. The measured neighbor advantage is plausible from shared technical vocabulary and should not trigger wording changes by itself.

decision: NO CONTENT DRIFT ACTION. Retain current Q9 wording and theory; do not optimize text to reduce scanner similarity.
limits: This is a disclosed, targeted manual review of supplied current Q9/Q6 snapshots, not a new blind acceptance of Q9.
No independent recomputation of scanner similarity or source hashes was performed; hashes are reported as supplied.
No repository, index, seed, theory, or Phase A artifacts were changed.
